grh_f5749544e8bf76a5b78a.title: Spellbound
paragraphs: Psychoanalyst Constance Peterson falls in love with the newly arrived Dr. Edwards, then discovers that the man is an amnesiac impostor who cannot remember his own identity and fears he may have murdered the real Edwards. Constance follows him when he flees and, with her old mentor Dr. Brulov, uses his dreams and phobias to recover the buried memories behind his guilt. He finally remembers that he is John Ballantine, an Army veteran whose childhood trauma came from accidentally causing his brotherâ€™s fatal fall, and that Dr. Edwards died during a skiing trip at Gabriel Valley. A bullet in Edwardsâ€™s body seems to condemn John after all, but Constance interprets the final symbols in his dream and realizes that retiring hospital chief Dr. Murchison had followed Edwards to the resort and shot him. She confronts Murchison, talks her way past his gun, and calls the police, clearing John and freeing the couple to marry.

grh_f5d076ee02cbffc24284.title: Blue Paradise
paragraphs: Young Rudy leaves Vienna, the Blue Paradise nightclub and flower girl Mitzi for a new life in America, promising that he will never forget either of them. Twenty-four years later he returns convinced that Vienna and his old love must still be waiting. His friends secretly recreate the vanished nightclub for one night, but Rudy eventually learns that Mitzi married his old friend Hampel and that the young woman who reminds him of her is their daughter Gaby. Accepting that he has been living in memory, Rudy chooses to celebrate the present and thanks his friends for giving him one more night in his Blue Paradise.

grh_f5c84ef10d6e9df5094a.title: Trilby
paragraphs: Young painter Billy Bagot loves Trilby, a Paris laundry girl with little confidence in her voice, but hypnotist Svengali takes control of her and transforms her into a celebrated singer while cutting Billy out of her life. Years later Billy finds her performing under Svengali's name. Svengali dies in the orchestra pit and the trance collapses, leaving Trilby unable to remember her career or sing on command. Billy helps her recover her own voice with a song from their past and promises a love stronger than Svengali's control.

grh_f5316e105587959b6784.title: It's in the Bag
paragraphs: Aboard the Orient Express, Harry talks a Greek traveler into buying a bundle of Yugoslav banknotes at a steep discount, then secretly tips border police that the man is carrying counterfeit money. The scheme briefly lands Harry in jail as well, until officials verify the notes and apologize. Back on the train, a veiled woman and her accomplice steal the suitcase containing Harry's cash by nesting it inside a larger bag and throwing the larger case from the train in a tunnel. Their plan backfires when the bag knocks the waiting accomplice unconscious. Police recover the money and identify the pair as dangerous agents, but instead of returning Harry's cash they confiscate it and reward his supposed heroism with a medal.

grh_f5ce7dfda3992d6fb84f.title: See Naples and Live
paragraphs: In prewar Naples, Harry plans to steal a valuable emerald locket worn by wealthy Mrs. Donaldson and cuts his dangerous partner Rubio out of the deal. Harry engineers an introduction to Mrs. Donaldson and her hired companion Amy Collins, then becomes genuinely attracted to Amy while arranging to drug Mrs. Donaldson and remove the locket during a moonlit visit to Pompeii. Rubio interrupts and tries to take the jewel, but police arrive and arrest him, leaving Harry looking like the hero who saved Mrs. Donaldson. Amy has seen enough to understand Harry's real purpose and quietly ends their budding romance. Harry loses both the emerald and Amy, receiving only a modest reward for his apparent bravery.

paragraphs: A young woman held by three criminals prays for help while her captors wait for another killer to arrive and dispose of her.
